correctness.summary: Zhang--Zhou prove the pointwise tensor inequality Hess(v)-|grad v|g>0 for v=-sqrt(u). Dividing its tangential restriction by |grad v| gives second fundamental form greater than the induced metric on every regular level. The unique nondegenerate minimum follows from positive Hessian and horo-convexity of the domain. For the level-flow vector field grad(v)/|grad v|^2, direct differentiation of transported tangent lengths and of log|grad v| gives strict rate greater than 1/|grad v|; integration yields the stated metric, Jacobian, gradient, and area expansion bounds. The signs and comparison direction agree with geodesic spheres in hyperbolic space.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The Zhang--Zhou preprint supplies the tensor inequality but does not state the torsion-level horo-convexity or exponential level-flow expansion package located here. Its discussion of horo-convex superlevel sets concerns the first Dirichlet eigenfunction in dimension two. Grossi--Provenzano already cover uniqueness and nondegeneracy of the torsion maximum in the hyperbolic plane, so that fact is excluded from the originality claim. Searches using synonymous torsion, hyperbolic, horo-convex level-set, principal-curvature, horosphere, and gradient-flow terminology found no matching all-dimensional metric/Jacobian/gradient expansion statement. Because the motivating preprint is recent, later revisions or unindexed parallel observations remain a residual risk.

value.summary: The result converts a strong analytic tensor estimate into a geometric comparison theorem: all regular torsion levels lie strictly beyond the horospherical curvature threshold and the canonical outward level flow expands tangent geometry faster than horospherical normal flow along its own path length. This yields a nested spherical foliation and quantitative metric, hypersurface-area, and gradient growth between arbitrary separated levels.

limitations: The result inherits strict horo-convexity and the small-diameter bound diam(Omega)<=1/(2 sqrt(n)).
No converse or removal of the diameter restriction is proved.
No explicit dimension-only positive gap above principal curvature 1 is obtained.
The two-dimensional uniqueness and nondegeneracy of the torsion maximum is prior work and is not claimed as new.
The motivating preprint is very recent, so later revisions or unindexed parallel observations may overlap.
Cross-model review has not been performed.
